intro_line: Moorish palaces and winding white lanes beneath snowy mountain peaks.
intro: Granada rewards slow walkers with palaces, tea houses, and Alhambra views at sunset, plus tapas bars along steep, winding lanes. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
transit_facts: One metro line runs in Granada. A single ticket costs about €1.65 (Nov 2024). A rechargeable green travel card costs €1.50 at tobacco shops and needs at least €5 of credit.
Local buses cover most sights. Alhambra Buses (C30 to the Alhambra, C31 to Albayzin, C34 to Sacromonte) cost €1.60 per trip (Nov 2024). Multi-trip cards cost €5, €10 or €20.
Taxis are easy to find. Ride apps such as Uber or Cabify: check locally.
Driving in the centre is restricted. Camera-enforced limits apply, so park outside the historic core or use a garage such as Parking HH Maristas.
Walking is the best way to see the old quarters, but streets are steep, narrow and uneven. Buses help on the hills.
No ferry service applies to Granada.

airports.name: Federico Garcia Lorca Airport
airports.note: Small regional airport with domestic and a few budget international flights, about 15 km west of the centre.

options.to: Gran Via de Colon (opposite the cathedral) or Palacio de Congresos
options.note: Runs about 11 times a day per route and is often timed to plane arrivals.

options.to: Granada Bus Station (north of the city)
options.note: Faster route; transfer to a local bus or taxi from there.
Quoted fare; use the official taxi rank outside arrivals.
Availability at the airport can be limited; confirm before you fly.

airports.name: Málaga-Costa del Sol Airport
airports.note: Main budget-airline hub about 130 km south-west of Granada, with far more international routes.

options.mode: Train (Cercanías to María Zambrano station, then Renfe with change at Bobadilla)
options.note: Cheapest option, but the connection at Bobadilla takes planning.
Direct coaches run on set times; book ahead in peak season.
Expensive for this distance; agree the fare or use the metered rank.
Often cheaper than trains or buses in Andalusia, but book in advance.
